main_text.p: corripi:in Germania & Mifia raró elephan-ticos uideri,& apud Scythas laḉtis potato-res nullos feré.Refert etiá Plinius lib.Natu-ralis historiæ uicefimo sexto, hunc asfeḉtū ante Pompei Magni ætaꝛem non accidisse in Italia: Ægypti peculiare esse hoc malū: & cūm in reges incidit populis funebre. Quippe(inquit) in balineis solia tempera-batur humano sanguine ad medicinam eā. Et hic quidem morbus celeriter in Italia re-stinctus est,sicuti & ille, quē gemursam ap-pellauere prisci, inter digitos pedum nas-centem nomine obliterato. Narrat quo-que Cornelius Celsus Latinorum medico Cap.2.rum princeps, lib. de re Medica tertio,ele-phantiasi suo tempore pene ignotam fuis-se in Italia: quòd certè nihil mirari oportet, quum sit locus temperatus. In nostra quo-que Gallia,& in ea præsertim,quæ Narbo-nensis dicitur raró uident elephãtici,duas ob causas: primùm quòd temperata sit re-gio,deinde quòd indigenæ non indulgeãt gulæ. Verù qui littora maris incolunt, huic malo admodum obnoxij sunt ob nimium piscium recentium,atque sale conditorum esum. Hi nanq; pisces salsam pituitam gig-nunt, illi uerò albam & crassam, unde illic uari-

page.notes: Marginal "Cap.2." at left is a printed reference, placed beside the paragraph at the line where "rum princeps" begins. The initial "C" of "Cap." is printed in italic. The text is set in long s throughout; transcribed as printed with s, which the instructions require to be plain s. Lines near "phantiasi" show a faint ink or show-through mark over "phantiasi suo" and at the far left margin ("Lu" in pencil or stain) which was not transcribed. The last line ends in a hyphenated word "uari-" continuing on the next page. The catchword and signature are not visible.
